Section 2: Eligibility and General Information

The DRC provides accommodations for students with documented disabilities that substantially limit one or more major life activities. Eligibility is determined on a case-by-case basis through an interactive process involving the student, DRC staff, and relevant documentation from qualified professionals.

Students seeking accommodations must:

1. Submit a DRC application form (available online or in person at the DRC office).
2. Provide current documentation of the disability from a licensed professional (e.g., physician, psychologist, or other qualified evaluator).
3. Meet with a DRC coordinator to discuss specific needs and reasonable accommodations.

Accommodations are not retroactive. They begin only after the plan is approved and the student has notified their instructors through the DRC's online portal.

### 10.3 How Note-Taking Assistance Is Arranged

The arrangement of note-taking assistance follows a structured process. At the beginning of each semester, the student must complete a Note-Taking Request Form for each course in which they wish to receive this accommodation. The form is available on the DRC student portal or in paper format at the LSC front desk. The student should submit the form no later than the end of the first week of classes to ensure timely placement of a note-taker.

Once the form is received, the LSC will contact the course instructor to confirm enrollment and to request a class roster. The LSC then identifies potential note-takers from the roster, typically selecting students who have previously demonstrated strong note-taking skills or who have volunteered for this role. If no volunteer is identified within the first two weeks, the LSC may ask the instructor to recommend a student or to make a general announcement to the class.

Note-taking Assistance note-taking assistance provider LSC (Learning Support Center). Record status: current.

Note-takers are compensated for their work. The compensation rate is $12.00 per class session for which they provide notes, paid biweekly through the university payroll system. Note-takers are expected to submit their notes within 24 hours of each class session. The LSC reviews the notes for legibility, completeness, and accuracy before forwarding them to the student through the secure LSC Notes Portal.

If a note-taker is unable to attend a class session, they are expected to notify the LSC in advance whenever possible. In such cases, the LSC may arrange for a backup note-taker from a pool of trained alternates, or the student may be offered a recording device for that session. The student should check the Notes Portal regularly, as notes may be posted at varying times depending on the note-taker's schedule.

- Informing the DRC and LSC of any schedule changes, including course drops or adds, within one week of the change.

**The LSC is responsible for:**
- Recruiting, training, and supervising note-takers.

- Conducting a mid-semester quality review of notes for each course, soliciting feedback from the student.

**The Instructor is responsible for:**
- Cooperating with the LSC in identifying note-takers from the class roster.
- Allowing the note-taker to share notes without penalty, as this is a sanctioned accommodation.

A reduced course load allows a student to enroll in fewer credit hours than the standard full-time
load while maintaining full-time enrollment status for the purposes of financial aid, scholarships,
health insurance, and athletic eligibility. This accommodation is intended for students whose
disability-related symptoms or treatment schedules make it difficult to manage a full academic
schedule.

The DRC provides accommodations for students with documented disabilities that substantially limit one or more major life activities. Extended Time on Exams has an extended time multiplier of 1.5 times. Record status: current. This multiplier applies to all timed assessments listed above and is effective for the duration of the 2024-2025 academic year.

Important implementation notes:

- The time multiplier is applied to the standard time allotted to the entire class. For example, if a quiz is designed for 30 minutes, the student will receive 45 minutes.

- For final exams, the student is expected to begin the exam at the same time as the rest of the class, unless an alternative time has been approved in writing by the DRC.

- The student is responsible for communicating with the instructor and the DRC testing center regarding exam scheduling. The student should schedule exams at least 48 hours in advance, excluding weekends and university holidays.

If a note-taker is unable to attend a class session, they are expected to notify the LSC in advance whenever possible. In such cases, the LSC may arrange for a backup note-taker from a pool of trained alternates, or the student may be offered a recording device for that session. **The Instructor is responsible for:**

- Allowing the note-taker to share notes without penalty, as this is a sanctioned accommodation.

Good questions. Tutoring through the Student Success Center is completely separate from DRC accommodations. You don't need to report it to us, and you don't need to disclose your accommodations to the tutoring center unless you want to – it's totally your call. The only thing to keep in mind is that tutoring is not a substitute for an accommodation, so if you feel like you need more support in a class, let me know and we can look at whether the current plan is working.

The drop-in hours are first come, first served, so if you go, I'd suggest getting there a few minutes early. The group sessions are a little more structured – you sign up for a specific time slot.

Hope that helps.

Best,
